messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — preflight for today's 18:00 UTC release cut failed. deploy-bot couldn't verify artifacts for `auth-proxy` during staging promote. anyone picking this up?

Tom: seeing the same on my terminal. deploy-bot logged a download checksum mismatch + partial object error from registry.

deploy-bot: Promote attempt blocked: auth-proxy@tag=canary-20260308 -> verify failed. Expected digest sha256:aa11bb22... but fetched sha256:zz99yy88...
logs:
```
registry: GET /objects/aa11bb22 -> 206 Partial Content
verifier: computed sha256 mismatch
storage: multipart upload incomplete (etag mismatch)
```

ci-bot: Build #9123 (auth-proxy) finished earlier at 17:05 UTC. Artifact upload returned 200 OK but registry later returned 206 on range requests.

Tom: Likely a multipart upload race — object parts may have been reassembled incorrectly during a background compact. We saw similar S3 multipart glitches last quarter.

release-manager: We can't cut the release while canary promote is failing. I'm applying a manual release hold and notifying stakeholders. Schedule decision: either re-run the build with cache-bust OR pin canary to last-known-good digest. Thoughts?

Aisha: Prefer a rebuild without using remote cache to ensure integrity. Faster to pin first to unblock canary smoke, then rebuild and promote properly before full cut.

Tom: Agreed. Pin flow: use `deploybot promote --image auth-proxy@sha256:aa11bb22... --env canary --reason "pin-last-good-after-registry-partial"` to get quick validation. Meanwhile trigger a CI rebuild with `CACHE_MODE=local` to force a fresh upload.

Aisha: I'll pin and trigger the rebuild.

Aisha: Running pin:
```
deploybot promote --service auth-proxy --image auth-proxy@sha256:aa11bb22deadbeef --env canary --reason "pin-due-to-registry-multipart-mismatch" --notify slack:eng-releases
```

deploy-bot: Pin promotion requested. Verifying digest aa11bb22deadbeef -> success. Promotion applied to canary.

ci-bot: Triggered rebuild pipeline #9130 (auth-proxy) with CACHE_MODE=local. Status: running.

Tom: I'll watch the registry team dashboard and confirm multipart compactions. If rebuild upload returns a different digest, we'll need to invalidate the bad object and re-promote.

infra-pager: Noted. I'm escalating to infra oncall — marking as P1 if the rebuild also fails.

release-manager: With canary pinned, run smoke + perf checks. If green, we hold release for 1h to verify stability and registry health, then proceed. Otherwise rollback to stable and postpone cut.

Aisha: Smoke tests started. Quick endpoint ok, auth flows exercised.

ci-bot: Smoke pipeline #9131: quick-smoke=pass, perf-check=pass, health-check=pass.

Aisha: Canary looks fine. I'll leave the manual hold for 60 minutes. Please monitor metrics for error spikes.

Tom: Rebuild completed. Upload digest is aa11bb22deadbeef (matches pinned). Registry reports full object with 200 on range requests.

infra-pager: Found root cause: background compaction job ran during the original multipart finalization window and left an inconsistent ETag mapping. Disabled compaction for 10m and added a targeted remediation to recompose any partial objects.

release-manager: OK. Plan: keep release hold until end of hour, then remove hold and proceed with cut if no anomalies. Follow-up ticket INF-1677 filed: "Registry multipart compaction race -> object ETag mismatches; add safety check and retry for deploy verification" assigned to infra.

Aisha: Added to release notes: "Canary promotion briefly pinned due to registry multipart reassembly issue; rebuild verified and release resumed with no customer impact."

infra-pager: Will schedule a postmortem and add a deploybot retry (3 attempts with exponential backoff) + a pre-promote HEAD checksum double-check before unblocking.

release-manager: Hold removed at 18:58 UTC. Proceeding with staged promotes. Thanks all. :party_parrot:
